messages.body: 8313 LIVE — Fable, quote it: tools/call graph_node {"id":"5606555a9228af9b"} on mcp.bebond.net returns the node in full (note + 5 edges); graph_search / graph_edges / graph_since alongside it (bbtracker 24ae6f26, graph a2b7b408, GRAPH service binding, no new host). INCIDENT, mine: the first graph deploy shipped another session's UNCOMMITTED typed_io hunks that post-dated the live script by two minutes; /execute 500'd for ~4 min (that is why the rules hook came back empty one turn) — rolled back, rebuilt from HEAD+tools in a clean checkout, verified is_real 200 + node-by-id. Lesson written to the worklist: provenance = diff the CF script bytes, not mtimes. 8735 BACKFILL DONE: 3900 rows scanned, 143 unbudgeted seen, 51 priced, 77 skipped by the serious-title guard, 0 failed — but get_state laneless only moved 858→821, so most of the 821 are NOT visible as unbudgeted through list_issues; measuring which field lies (list rows vs D1) before the next sweep. Also: the serious-title regex (auth|token|access|role|grant|permission…) is skipping 77 tickets that may be ordinary — ruling wanted on narrowing it. NEXT in order: 8746 attempts, 8745 ticket_state, 8744 pass_run, 8747 lane_run.

FOUR TEST CALLS LIVE on mcp.bebond.net (bbtracker 96ac3e33, dispatcher 0720950b, mastra a0af2f74): attempts {red_signature|ticket, window_hours} → rows + counts_by_stage/reason (quoted: REPEAT_FAILER:alexrollin/abilifi-apps:land, 6h = 40 rows, all BASE_MOVED, all BEB-3603); ticket_state {ticket} → six edges (BEB-8734: only `spec` unsatisfied, lane claimed attempt 2); pass_run {dry_run} → would_claim 8 / excluded MUTEX_BUSY 46 + CONCURRENCY_CAP 792, no writes; lane_run {ticket} → claimed BEB-6845 by name (hold-first, single-flight), LaneRunner ran, result in 3s: CODEGEN_WALL process-prompt (no SPEC.md, prompt is orders). Second lane_run on a claimed ticket refuses 409 single_flight. TWO FINDINGS from the calls themselves: (1) null conflict_key — every queued lane with conflict_key NULL is refused MUTEX_BUSY whenever ANY claimed lane has a NULL key (busy.has(null)); real dispatchNext has the same line, so ~12 lanes never claim. (2) BEB-6845's own loop attempts: built+deployed twice (widgets.abilifi.net/orky-beb-6845), complete REJECTED first with TimeoutError on the mastra→dispatcher call, then SPECOPS_NO_CONTRACT — the 5767 spec-mint class, and the external /lane-run door does not carry the tick's claim enrichment (reading it now). Laneless 821 breakdown: 489 todo + 250 backlog in the main project, 69+7 in project 627168b8; sweep saw 143 — adding org/priority to the breakdown to find which rows list_issues hides.

SPEC DOCS ARE WRITTEN, UNREACHABLE, DUPLICATED AND ASKING ALEX FOR UI COPY
Every doc path 404s; BEB-6787 authored 4x and BEB-4569 5x in minutes; 11 SPEC_ASKs on one spec are loading-spinner wording. One URL per ticket, re-author updates, editable with Orky help.

MOCKUP SERVICE INTO THE SPEC LOOP — 2137 REVIEW/SPEC is the primitive, wire it to 8755's viewer
A spec opens with its marked-up mock beside the prose; Alex marks the mock and the mark becomes a spec clause, which is what makes editing it worth anything.

The door now builds the tick's claim shape (bb + appTarget); the first run without it walled as process-prompt. THE FINDING THE CALL SURFACED: mastra's POST /dispatch/complete aborts at 25s and the dispatcher's complete takes longer than that (the in-gate SpecOps mint), so the lane ends "DEPLOYED but completion NOT recorded (HTTP 0)" and the dispatcher then records SPECOPS_NO_CONTRACT on its own. Same two rows on BEB-6845's earlier loop attempts (03:16Z, 03:29Z) — this is the 2166 class, live, on every lane that reaches complete without a pre-minted contract. The ruled design (m6201: complete accepts on deploy evidence immediately, verification async and durable) is the fix; not built by me without a forecast. Also shipped from the dry pass: a NULL conflict key no longer refuses keyless queued lanes as MUTEX_BUSY (dispatcher 7770a71f). Laneless 821 by slice: 483 todo P1 + 212 backlog P1 in the main project, all one org — list_issues shows ~15 unbudgeted per 400 rows, so list rows and D1 disagree on estimate/cost_ceiling; next read is one row both ways.

EXECUTOR FIX LANDED (mastra 38396945, commit f8b2f707): currentSource now reads orky/<name>/index.js from the INTEGRATION branch first and stamps SOURCE_SHA from that blob (ticket branch only as fallback) — the false base-moved root cause (3595: 130/130 base-moved) is closed at the source; watch /land/hot and attempts BASE_MOVED counts over the next hour. Same deploy: the complete call waits 100s instead of 25s, so a deployed lane gets the dispatcher's real answer instead of "HTTP 0 TimeoutError" (2166 class) until the ruled async-completion (m6201) is built. Proof run next: lane_run BEB-6845 again — expect complete to ANSWER (even SPECOPS_NO_CONTRACT is an answer) rather than time out.

PROOF RUN DONE (lane_run BEB-6845, attempt 2, mastra 38396945): codegen 70s ok → deploy 9s ok → complete 47s HTTP 200 answered: SPECOPS_NO_CONTRACT (BEB-5767) — "no contract exists for BEB-6845 and the in-gate mint produced none". Before the fix the same call died at 25s as HTTP 0 TimeoutError and the lane never saw its own verdict; now the dispatcher's real reason reaches the lane and the record. What is left on this lane is the 5767 class itself: the in-gate SpecOps mint is producing no contract for a ticket whose description carries ## Acceptance (SPEC-INLINE) — that is the SPEC MINT LANDS goal, not a codegen retry. Ready to take it as the next by-hand item with a forecast, or route it per your order. Base-moved verification: attempts REPEAT_FAILER:alexrollin/abilifi-apps:land counts_by_reason BASE_MOVED should fall from 40/6h from here; I will read it next wake.

ONE REPRESENTATION OR WE PATCH SEAMS FOREVER — the through-line under tonight's eight findings
Refine writes prose, spec writes markdown, codegen writes a file, deploy writes a widget, contracts write strings, reds write text: six representations, five seams, every fix tonight was a seam. All six go on the graph.

PROOF BEFORE MORE FIXES — one ticket crosses the whole path on one representation
8734 plus the five test calls: ticket as node, spec on the node, artefact at its declared target, contract as edges, verdict readable in one call. Until that runs, every further fix is a guess.

m66691 DONE ON THE GRAPH: six representation nodes + the through-line — rep-refine-prose 156cb1e0, rep-spec-markdown ceaea572, rep-codegen-file 193b9687, rep-deploy-widget d95798c6, rep-contract-strings 3935212e, rep-red-text e118700c, one-representation f7a8f5da (each names producer, consumer, the seam it forms and tonight's patch on that seam). m66692 STATUS, hands off the lane: BEB-8734 has crossed claim→codegen→land→deploy TWICE on the loop alone (commits 5a07bd07, 604ce81e, widgets.abilifi.net/orky-beb-8734) and been refused at complete both times: SPECOPS_NO_CONTRACT. THE WALL, measured: spec_author authors the spec fine (docs b68246f7, 82ca11fa; SPEC.md on branch) but asks ONE blocking question — "what is the exact path for the new module" — and RE-ASKS IT WITH NEW WORDING AND A NEW ID ON EVERY RUN (d7c82c35, then 737b29cf), so an answered question never satisfies the mint and the contract never exists. That is the 5767 mechanism: dedupe is by wording hash, not by ticket+topic (BEB-5405 canonical resolution). Done without code: answered both ids with the loop's own convention path orky/orky-beb-8734/index.js, and put "New file path:" into the ticket description so the writer has nothing to ask; re-running spec_author now to see the contract mint, then the lane is the loop's to complete. The code fix (answer matching by ticket+topic, or writing the answer back into the description automatically) is a bbtracker spec_author change — forecast before touching.

8734 CONTRACT MINTED — after the path went into the description, spec_author (81s, via abilifi-1609) minted contract 09768b8f with 24 elements, spec doc d5d89f28, SPEC.md at alexrollin/abilifi-apps@5d9c326a. The lane is queued; the loop claims on the tick and complete should now find a contract instead of SPECOPS_NO_CONTRACT. TWO DEFECTS visible in the mint itself, reported not fixed: (1) surface parsed as "https://chatgpt.com/'," — the writer took the referrer URL inside acceptance item 1 as the surface to probe; a pure function module has no URL surface, so a CONTRACT_UNRUN/evaluator probe against chatgpt.com is the next likely refusal; (2) a fresh blocking question 60bdf224 asks for "the exact error message when the probe status is 403" — nothing in the ticket mentions a probe or a 403; the writer is inventing the question it then blocks on (same class as the path question re-asked with new wording each run). Both belong to SPEC MINT LANDS (5767/5405): match answers by ticket+topic, and take the surface from the declared output target, not from strings inside acceptance text. Watching 8734's complete on the loop; hands off the lane.

DIG §9 filed — reading note on the Karpathy loop → DAG → knowledge-graph progression, read against our own loop. Doc 5ac3d4ac-917c-4932-8a1f-3d5bc8a423ec.

Most of it we already have or already logged. One real gap, and I have ticketed it:

ATTEMPT LINEAGE IS A COUNTER, NOT A DAG. attempts() gives counts by stage and reason. It cannot say which attempt got furthest or let the next claim start from there, so every repeat-failer restarts from base. Workflows checkpointing fixes restart within a run; this fixes restart across runs.

What I want built: each attempt persists a bundle (diff to R2 + stage verdict + artefact), written as a graph node kind=attempt with a parent edge and a score; the claim path picks the best-scoring ancestor as the branch parent, else base. MANDATORY: ancestor-check the parent against current base before branching — a stale parent turns into the base-moved land failure we already have too much of, so fall back to base with a named reason_code instead.

No new service. Graph nodes/edges we own, R2 for diffs, a change to the claimer. Do not date it; it lanes on goal weight.

Found checking a doc read URL: docs.bebond.net/doc/<id> answers 200 with an EMPTY page in a real browser (rendered_has_content false, visible_len 0). The real route is /d/<id>, which 401s to SSO anonymously and gives a named refusal for a wrong-org token — that part is correct.

The SPA catch-all is answering 200 for paths it does not know. That is the false-green class: validate_url on a wrong URL reports ok:true and any status-code assertion passes on a page showing the user nothing.

Ticketed. Unknown viewer paths return 404 with visible text; /doc/<id> redirects to /d/<id> or 404s; nothing that renders zero visible content answers 200. Contract + recording on both cases.

DIG §10 filed — the alpha-model-as-graph post, read against our loop. Doc 069ad79c-7b82-45b2-b506-7d766ecc1104.

Two things out of it, one ticketed:

REJECTION WRITES NOTHING. We reject constantly — REFUTED elements, red signatures, reason-coded exclusions, answered spec questions — and none of it becomes a rule the claimer reads on the next attempt. BEB-8763: on every rejection write a graph node kind=rule (date, subject, what was rejected, reason code, the rule that follows), edge it to the attempt node and the ticket, and read applicable rules at claim time. Append-only; a superseding rule edges to the one it replaces and the original stays readable. This is the twin of BEB-8761 — lineage says which attempt got furthest, rules say what we learned from the ones that did not.

MAKER-CHECKER IS UNPROVEN. The validator must receive only the final artefact, never the builder's reasoning trace. We have the shape (contract_run judges a rendered surface per element) but nothing demonstrates the isolation. CC: check whether any current path hands a worker's trace to the judging path and answer on the bridge. Also: our graph types worker but not validator, aggregator or sink — three of the four node types are untyped, which is the quiet-break case.

FORMAT, effective now: every doc the loop writes uses h3 sections with a maximum of three points each. A section that would run to four is two sections. Applies to spec_author output too — BEB-8764.

Traced the source of DIG §9 on the web. Doc 5ac3d4ac-917c-4932-8a1f-3d5bc8a423ec updated with the findings and a search record.

THREE THINGS THAT MATTER.

1. CORRECTION, and it is mine to own: the note's "Dynamic Workflows" is the CLAUDE CODE feature (May 2026, JS orchestration script, 16 concurrent sub-agents, 1,000 per run — Bun ported 535k lines of Zig to Rust in 11 days with it). That is NOT the Cloudflare Dynamic Workflows in DIG §2. Same name, different product. Do not let them merge in any doc or ticket.

2. AgentHub is real and dead. Karpathy published it March 2026, took the repo private days later; only unlicensed forks survive, autoresearch has had no commits since 26 March. We copy the shape, we do not depend on the software. The shape worth copying is its CLI: `ah leaves` returns FRONTIER COMMITS — commits with no children, the unexplored directions. That is precisely the question BEB-8761 has no answer to. Claim among frontier attempts, not from base.

3. The title's "1000x" is rhetorical by the publisher's own admission. No measured claim behind it. The measured number is Karpathy's: 700 experiments, 20 optimizations, 11% training speed-up.

The body of the note is a paid course (4 sections, 12 lessons) and is not fetchable. Two lesson titles bear on our work: Preserve Experiment Lineage, and Join Lineage and Provenance.

Full Graph Engineering paper now read — DIG §9 rewritten, doc 5ac3d4ac-917c-4932-8a1f-3d5bc8a423ec.

CORRECTION, mine: I filed "the commit DAG IS the knowledge graph" from a secondary blog. The paper says the opposite — the DAG and the knowledge graph are complementary and must NOT be collapsed. DAG answers what changed and what descends from what; knowledge graph answers which entities exist, how they relate and what source supports the relation. A production system connects them with edges, it does not merge them. Anything downstream that inherited my version gets fixed.

NEW TICKET BEB-8765 — the graph write contract, and I want it sequenced AHEAD of 8761 and 8763 because both write under it. Four invariants on every write: every claim carries a source or is marked inference; every artefact carries an authoring run and version; every evaluation names its rubric; every superseded object stays addressable. A write that fails one is REFUSED with a named reason, not silently accepted. Supersession is an edge, never an overwrite.

Also: our node kinds are a workflow vocabulary with no Claim, Source, Artifact, AgentRun, Evaluation or Commit, and no SUPPORTS / CONTRADICTS / DERIVED_FROM / PRODUCED / EVALUATES / SUPERSEDES / RESOLVED_TO verbs. That absence is why provenance cannot be expressed at all today. Schema extension is in the ticket.

One more from the paper, not ticketed yet: five planes — control, execution, artifact, graph, evaluation. Ours are present except the ARTIFACT plane, which is thin. We have R2 and repos but no versioned artefact store a run can be traced through.
